The rich culture of the forest nurtured by the blessings of the mountains, 'Forest Kyoto'. Please enjoy the captivating videos of the traditional culture nurtured by the forest and people in the six towns of the Forest Kyoto area.

■ Wachi Puppet Joruri (Kyotanba Town, Kyoto Prefecture)

The roots of Wachi Puppet Joruri date back about 150 years. It is said to have started as a pastime of puppet manipulation during the farming off-season. A unique feature is that a single person operates the puppets, which are usually handled by three people. The art, which integrates the roles of the tayu (narrator), shamisen player, and puppeteer, is a traditional skill that the region takes pride in. You can see it at regular performances at the Wachi Traditional Performing Arts Permanent Hall.

description:
Having received the blessings of the mountains and developed alongside the rich forests, 'Forest Kyoto'. Please enjoy the captivating videos of the traditional culture nurtured by the forest and people in the six towns of the Forest Kyoto area.

■Oso Shrine Tug-of-War (Yagi, Nantan City, Kyoto Prefecture)

This ritual has been passed down for over a thousand years, inspired by the story of a warrior who defeated a giant serpent that plagued the village. A net representing the serpent is pulled north and south across the torii gate, with the belief that if the south wins, rice will be abundant, and if the north wins, wheat will be abundant. The event is scheduled to be held on a Sunday in mid-January each year. Located in Yuki, Yagi Town, Nantan City, Kyoto Prefecture.

title: Fukuchiyama Ondo - Intangible Cultural Heritage of the Region, A Culture Nurtured by the Forest Awaits You
description: Fukuchiyama Ondo is characterized by the call of 'Dokkoi se, Dokkoi se!' and originates from the people who sang and danced while transporting timber and stones during the construction of Fukuchiyama Castle. It is still a beloved traditional dance performed at the Fukuchiyama Dokkoi Se Festival every year on August 14-16 and 24-25.

title: 【綾部市】#5 綾部太鼓～地域無形文化遺産 森育ちの文化が待っている～

title: 【Ayabe City】#5 Ayabe Taiko - The Intangible Cultural Heritage of the Region Awaits in the Forest-Grown Culture
description: Ayabe Taiko originated from the drums struck by the Kuki Navy, who were active in the Toba region, to inspire their soldiers. When Kuki Takaki, the grandson of Kuki Yoshitaka, became the first lord of the Ayabe domain, the powerful drums were passed down. They are showcased at events such as the Ayabe Hatsu Ebisu Festival, the Oomoto Setsubun Festival, and the Ayabe Tan no Kuni Festival.

title: 2021年度森の京都文化観光サポーターラジオ 第3回「丹波の漆かき」
description:
京都FM丹波のラジオ番組　「森の京都presents知っとる？伝統文化in 福知山」の放送音声です。森の京都文化観光サポーターが月1回福知山市の無形文化財を取り上げ、サポーターの目線で皆さまに紹介していきます。

 第3回目は【丹波の漆かき】
京都府福知山市夜久野町は古くから「丹波漆」が採れる日本でも有数の漆の産地です。そこには、日本の伝統産業を守り、受け継いでいく漆かき職人がいます。

 番組前半は漆の基礎知識編。
江戸時代に盛んだった漆かき、現在使われている漆は9割が輸入漆です。
この貴重な国産漆のスゴイをご紹介します！

後半は漆かき職人でNPO法人丹波漆の広報担当でもある山内耕祐さんをゲストに迎えお話しを伺います。漆との出会い、福知山移住のきっかけ、苦労されることや漆の魅力などをお聞きしました。爽やかな印象の山内さんの漆に対する熱い想いにサポーターも感動！

description:
This is the broadcast audio of the radio program "Mori no Kyoto presents Shittoru? Traditional Culture in Fukuchiyama" on Kyoto FM Tanba. The Mori no Kyoto Cultural Tourism Supporters introduce intangible cultural assets in Fukuchiyama from the perspective of supporters once a month.

 The third episode is about "Tamba Urushi (lacquer)". Yaku no Town in Fukuchiyama City, Kyoto Prefecture, has been one of Japan's leading lacquer-producing areas since ancient times, where lacquer craftsmen are preserving and passing on this traditional industry.

 The first half of the program covers the basics of lacquer. Lacquer tapping was popular during the Edo period, and currently, 90% of the lacquer used is imported. We will introduce the amazing qualities of this precious domestic lacquer!

 In the second half, we welcome guest Kousuke Yamauchi, a lacquer craftsman and public relations officer of the NPO Tamba Urushi, to talk about his encounter with lacquer, the reasons for moving to Fukuchiyama, the challenges he faces, and the charm of lacquer. The supporters were also moved by Yamauchi's passionate feelings towards lacquer, which left a refreshing impression!

description: 北海道の魅力的な観光スポットや観光資源を紹介するBEST HOKKAIDO。北海道の絶景景色を様々な角度から映像でお届けします。今回は、広尾町にある「サンタランド」をご紹介します。北海道十勝にある広尾町はサンタクロースの故郷ノルウェーのオスロ市が認めた国外初、日本で唯一のサンタランドです。サンタランドの活動拠点であるフログン市と友好交流提携を結び、サンタランドの基本理念「愛と平和、感謝と奉仕」に基づいたまちづくりを行っています。日本一早いクリスマス点灯式である「サンタランドツリー点灯式」が行われ、15万球のイルミネーションで彩る「サンタランドイルミネーション」は11月から楽しめます。また、2020年にはシンボルツリーとなるクリスマスツリーが植樹されました。カップルにオススメな場所です。

title: Hiroo Town Santa Land ／北海道の絶景景色 【BESTHOKKAIDO_VOL.123】
description: This time, we will introduce 'Santa Land' in Hiroo Town. Hiroo Town, located in Tokachi, Hokkaido, is the first SantaLand in Japan and the first outside Japan to be recognized by Oslo, Norway, the hometown of Santa Claus. We have formed a friendship and exchange partnership with Frogn City, the base of Santaland's activities, and are developing the town based on Santaland's basic philosophy of 'Love, Peace, Gratitude and Service.' The 'Santaland Tree Lighting Ceremony' is the earliest Christmas lighting ceremony in Japan, and the 'Santaland Illumination' with 150,000 lights can be enjoyed from November. Additionally, in 2020, a Christmas tree was planted as a symbol. This place is recommended for couples.

This time, I would like to introduce Lake Kutcharo in Hamatonbetsu Town. Kutcharo Lake is the northernmost Ramsar site in the country. It is an important stopover point for waterfowl migrating between Japan and Russia, and many migratory birds come here to rest their wings. Particularly in spring and fall, you can see thousands of swans and tens of thousands of ducks, and in winter you can also see the natural monuments white-tailed eagles and Steller's sea eagles.

Miyajima Swamp in Bibai City is famous for the large numbers of white-fronted geese that fly there every spring and fall. This small, shallow marsh with an area of 25 hectares and an average depth of 55 cm has been registered under the Ramsar Convention as an important staging area for white-fronted geese. From the observatory, you can also see the sandbar, also known as the 'Ryugu Kaido' that separates the lake and the sea, and the Shiretoko mountain range in the distance on a clear day. The observatory has three telescopes, and you can see every corner of Lake Saroma, and the view is first-class.

今回は、北海道開基百年を記念して1983年に開設された「Historical Village of Hokkaido」を紹介します。

明治から昭和初期にかけて建築された北海道各地の建造物を移築復元・再現した野外博物館です。
訪れる人たちに開拓当時の生活を体感的に理解してもらうことと、文化の流れを示す建造物を保存し、後世に永く伝えることを目的に開村しました。
村内は市街地・農村・山村・漁村の4エリアに分かれ、開拓当時にタイムスリップしたかのような景色が広がります。
開拓当時の文化を体験できる伝統遊具づくりやわら細工講習なども随時開催してます。

This time, we will introduce the 'Historical Village of Hokkaido', which was established in 1983 to commemorate the 100th anniversary of the founding of Hokkaido.

It is an open-air museum that relocates and restores buildings built in various parts of Hokkaido from the Meiji to early Showa eras.
It was opened to help visitors understand the life during the pioneering days and to preserve buildings that show the flow of culture for future generations.
The village is divided into four areas: Town, Farm Village, Mountain Village, and Fishing Village, creating a landscape that feels like a time slip back to the pioneering days.
Workshops on making traditional playground equipment and straw crafts are also held from time to time.

title: Kagoshima Prefecture Ibusuki City / Hiraki Shrine (Drone / iPhone 4K Shooting)
description: Hiraki Shrine is located in Kaimonju-cho, Ibusuki City, Kagoshima Prefecture. It is primarily dedicated to the deity Oohirume-muchi-no-mikoto, along with other ancestral gods of Amaterasu. Eight pillars of the imperial ancestors are also enshrined here. It has been deeply revered as a guardian deity of the southern Satsuma region and as the god of the ancestors who opened this area. Particularly, it is cherished by local fishermen as a guardian of traffic safety, maritime safety, and fishing. There is a statue of a divine horse in the precincts, and there are legends related to the divine horse. Additionally, you can see the symbol of Ibusuki, Mount Kaimon, behind the main shrine. Various types of ema (votive tablets) inspired by Mount Kaimon, the vermilion shrine, and the lush precincts are also available. It is said to bring benefits not only for traffic and maritime safety but also for warding off evil and bringing good fortune. Please visit Hiraki Shrine.

description: Ikeda Lake is the largest caldera lake in Kyushu, with a circumference of about 15 km and a maximum depth of 233 m. The lake is characterized by its mystical natural scenery and the tranquil landscapes surrounding it. It was formed over a long period due to volcanic eruptions that caused the ground to collapse about 5,700 years ago. The lake is home to the 'giant eel,' which can grow over 1.5 meters and is designated as a natural monument. There is also a legend that a mysterious creature called 'Issy' resides here. The lakeside is planted with flowers that bloom in every season, adding color to the scenery. On October 7, 2022, a facility called 'IKEDAKO PAX' was opened, featuring a café and a waterside deck. Please take your time to enjoy sightseeing around Ikeda Lake. At low tide, a sandy path appears, so be sure to visit Chirin Island. *Filming was done with special permission.

description: いぶすき元湯温泉は指宿温泉を代表する老舗の公衆浴場です。近隣には宿泊施設や砂むし温泉もあり、観光客の方も路地散策を楽しみながら立ち寄ることができます。

description: 香ばしく ふわふわ！鹿児島県指宿市の人気返礼品☆うなぎ鹿児島県は養鰻生産量日本一のうなぎ大国。南九州の温暖な気候とシラス台地の土壌でろ過された水で養殖された国産うなぎは身はふっくらして、臭みもなく、安全・安心・高品質の逸品です。他にも、「黒毛和牛」「黒豚」「完熟マンゴー」などオススメの返礼品をご紹介！

title: Sizzle! Ibusuki - Unagi
description: Fragrant and fluffy! Popular return gift from Ibusuki City, Kagoshima Prefecture ☆ Unagi. Kagoshima Prefecture is the largest producer of eel in Japan. The domestic eel, farmed in water filtered through the soil of the Shirasu plateau in the warm climate of southern Kyushu, is plump, odorless, and a safe, secure, and high-quality product. We also introduce recommended return gifts such as 'Kuroge Wagyu', 'Kurobuta', and 'Ripe Mango'!

description: 世界的にも珍しい「指宿砂むし温泉」の体験レポート！“砂むし”って一体どんな温泉なの？どんな格好で入るの？どんな感じで砂に埋もれるの？など、写真だけでは伝わらない砂むし温泉体験の模様をお届けします。ぜひ、ここでしか味わえない温泉の魅力を体感しに、指宿へおじゃったもんせ～

title: I Tried the Ibusuki Natural Sand Bath!
description: A report on the experience of the rare 'Ibusuki Sand Bath'! What kind of hot spring is 'sand bath'? What kind of clothes do you wear? What does it feel like to be buried in sand? We will deliver the experience of the sand bath that cannot be conveyed by photos alone. Please come to Ibusuki to experience the charm of this hot spring that can only be enjoyed here!

title: 【鹿児島県指宿市】ふるさとチョイス大感謝祭！初めての生配信はうまくいったのか？！
description: 「Furusato Choice Grand Thanksgiving Festival」のオンライン生配信動画です。砂むし温泉に入ったり、しゃぶしゃぶを食べたり、Ibusukiの魅力がぎゅぎゅっと詰まった内容となっています！クイズコーナーや砂の温かさを表現するための実験など、ワクワクが止まらない30分間に乞うご期待！！

title: Kagoshima Prefecture Ibusuki City: Furusato Choice Grand Thanksgiving Festival! Did the first live broadcast go well?!
description: This is a video of the 'Furusato Choice Grand Thanksgiving Festival' streamed live online. It features experiences like entering a sand bath and eating shabu-shabu, packed with the charm of Ibusuki! Look forward to 30 exciting minutes filled with a quiz corner and experiments to express the warmth of sand!

title: 【鹿児島県指宿市】「読めない、指宿」フル
description: 全国の約４割の人が読めないといわれる難読地名「指宿（いぶすき）」には、沸き立つ砂浜やテーブルの上でぐるぐる回るそうめんなど、ほかの地域では想像できない“読めない”素材が盛りだくさん！“読めない”を逆手にとって、指宿出身のお笑い芸人が「読めない、指宿」をテンポのいい曲調にあわせてコミカルに紹介♪インパクトのあるキャラクターと曲調は、脳内リピートされること間違いなし！

title: Ibusuki City, Kagoshima Prefecture: 'Ibusuki, Unreadable' Full
description: About 40% of people nationwide are said to be unable to read the difficult-to-read place name 'Ibusuki'. 'Unreadable, Ibusuki' is packed with 'unreadable' materials that you can't imagine in other regions, such as bubbling sandy beaches and somen noodles spinning on the table! Taking advantage of the 'unreadable', a comedian from Ibusuki comically introduces 'Unreadable, Ibusuki' to a catchy tune! The impactful characters and melody are sure to be stuck in your head!

title: Shimanami Citrus Paradise#ShimanamiConnect #VisitShimanami
description: I started the day with some delicious homemade citrus jams. The Shimanami Kaido really is a citrus paradise! The Hassaku daifuku tasted amazing. I recharged with refreshing juices, saw eye-catching clothing with fun citrus designs, and picked fruit with friendly local farmers.

title: しまなみ柑橘パラダイス
description: 私は美味しい自家製の柑橘ジャムで一日を始めました。しまなみ海道は本当に柑橘の楽園です！はっさく大福は素晴らしい味でした。私はさわやかなジュースでリフレッシュし、楽しい柑橘デザインの目を引く衣服を見て、地元の農家と一緒に果物を摘みました。

title: People of Shimanami #ShimanamiConnect #VisitShimanami
description: I met residents who were born and raised on the islands, as well as those who have recently moved there. Each encounter deepened my understanding of the significance of the region to them. Seeing the region through the eyes of locals highlighted the strong sense of community that connects everyone across the various islands. Are you ready to write your own Shimanami story?

title: しまなみの人々
description: 私は、島で生まれ育った住民や、最近移住してきた人々に出会いました。各々の出会いは、彼らにとってこの地域の重要性を深く理解させてくれました。地元の人々の目を通して地域を見ることで、さまざまな島々をつなぐ強いコミュニティの感覚が際立ちました。あなた自身のしまなみの物語を書く準備はできていますか？

title: Shimanami Stays#ShimanamiConnect #VisitShimanami
description: After spending the day exploring, I was ready to relax at one of the many cozy ryokan along the Shimanami Kaido. Thanks to the kindness of each innkeeper, I was able to learn more about the region and discover the places that locals frequent. Listening to their personal stories helped me build a deeper connection with the region.

title: Shimanami Stays#ShimanamiConnect #VisitShimanami
description: 一日中探索した後、私はしまなみ海道沿いの多くの快適な旅館の一つでリラックスする準備ができていました。各宿の親切のおかげで、地域についてもっと学び、地元の人々がよく訪れる場所を発見することができました。彼らの個人的な物語を聞くことで、地域とのより深い結びつきを築くことができました。

title: Sun, seas and sky, long the Shimanami Kaido Blue Line#ShimanamiConnect #VisitShimanami
description: I departed from Onomichi surrounded by other bikers eager to begin their journey. I followed the Blue Line along winding coastlines and through quaint villages, leisurely enjoying the sights along the way. The road led me to my final stop, Kirosan, just in time to see an unforgettable sunset.

title: 太陽、海、空、しまなみ海道の青いライン
description: 私は他のバイカーたちに囲まれて尾道を出発し、旅を始めることに興奮していました。青いラインに沿って曲がりくねった海岸線や素朴な村を通り抜けながら、道中の景色をゆっくり楽しみました。最終目的地のキロ山に到着したとき、忘れられない夕日を見ることができました。

title: Tastes of Shimanami #ShimanamiConnect #VisitShimanami
description: There was no shortage of delicious foods to keep me energized on my journey. I enjoyed all different types of flavors, from freshly brewed coffee, to sweet citrus desserts, to traditional rice balls. And of course no journey would be complete without some ice cream!

title: しまなみの味
description: この酸味のあるレモネードが私を活気づけ、自転車に乗る準備をさせてくれました！

title: Shimanami Cafe Society #ShimanamiConnect #VisitShimanami
しまなみカフェ社会 #ShimanamiConnect #VisitShimanami
description: どこをサイクリングしても、美味しいカフェから遠くない場所にいました。スタイリッシュなガレットから、島のおばあさんが愛情を込めて作ったシンプルなおにぎりまで、すべてのカフェには独自の料理と魅力的な雰囲気がありました。すべての立ち寄り先で、フレンドリーなカフェのオーナーたちの温かさを感じました。

title: Connect with the slow life of island life along the Shimanami Kaido
description: The 70km-long Shimanami Kaido in Japan is one of the world’s most beautiful and most accessible bike routes. Island-hopping across the Seto Inland Sea between Honshu and Shikoku via the route's famous bridges is one of Japan's most unforgettable experiences. With a large fleet of bikes available for rent and cycle terminals located all along a route that is clearly marked by the now iconic 'Blue Line,' spending a few days exploring this gorgeous part of Japan is stress-free and safe. And, of course, meeting and chatting with the people of Shimanami along the way is a highlight of any visit.

title: 空ノ里（四國， 德島）
description: 昔、徳島県市区に住む人々はこの高地を「空」と呼んでいました。空の夜空には、個人住宅の蛍が星空のように輝いています。Sora-no-satoは四国市中心の「西阿波・剣山・吉野川観光区」（美馬市、三好市、つるぎ町、東みよし町）に位置しています。自然、歴史と文化、伝説と伝承、独特の食文化と伝統芸能を代表する日本の主要な観光地の一つです。25年の歴史を持ち、地域には190の民宿があり、同時に400人を収容できます。Sora-no-satoの多くの教育民宿は山の斜面に密接に位置し、独特の文化的景観を形成しています。山地、小丘、石造りの家々などの独特の風景は日本の原始的な景観であり、桃原郷とも呼ばれています。学生たちは家族の一員として歓迎され、茶摘み、玉ねぎ、ジャガイモの収穫などの持続可能な自給自足の農業に共に従事します。収穫した季節の野菜や山菜を使って、共に田舎料理を作り、家族の食事を通じて心と心の交流を行います。日本の最も厳しい生活を豊かな生活に変える方法を学びます。

title: Sora-no-sato (Shikoku, Tokushima)
description: A long time ago, the people living in the urban area of Tokushima Prefecture referred to this high-altitude area as 'Sora'. In the night sky of Sora, the fireflies from private homes shine brightly like stars. Sora-no-sato is located in the 'Nishiawa-Tsurugisan-Yoshinogawa Tourist Area' in the center of Shikoku (Mima City, Miyoshi City, Tsurugi Town, Higashimiyoshi Town). It is one of Japan's leading tourist areas, representing nature, history and culture, legends and folklore, as well as unique food culture and traditional performing arts. With a history of 25 years, there are 190 private accommodations in the area that can accommodate 400 people at the same time. Many educational guesthouses of Sora-no-sato are located in villages close to the mountains, forming a unique cultural landscape. The unique scenery of mountains, small hills, stone houses, etc., is Japan's original landscape, also known as Momohara Village. Students are welcomed as family members and engage together in sustainable self-sufficient agriculture, such as tea picking, onion, and potato harvesting. Using the seasonal vegetables and wild vegetables harvested, we cook rural cuisine together and exchange hearts and minds through family meals. You will learn how to turn one of Japan's harshest lives into a prosperous life.

title: Largo
description: This is a farmhouse in the mountains of the Nishi-Awa region in Tokushima Prefecture, recognized as a Globally Important Agricultural Heritage System (GIAHS) area, welcoming educational travel. Certified as a 'Tokushima Agricultural, Forestry and Fisheries Minpaku', we offer hospitality with local ingredients and seasonal mountain vegetables, as well as herb sweets. Let's think about how people have protected and walked this road.

title: 丹波山観光PR 武田家の隠し金山探検
description: During the era of Takeda Shingen, it is said that a gold mine magistrate was placed in Tanbayama Village for the mining of the Kurokawa Gold Mine. Remnants of that time remain in the village, and you will head towards the gold mine ruins with a guide. Please walk along the stream, which is also a source of water for Tokyo, and feel the blessings of water with all your senses.

title: Exploration of the Hidden Gold Mine of the Takeda Family in Tanbayama
description: 武田信玄の時代、黒川金山採掘のため、丹波山村に金山奉行が置かれていたと伝えられています。村内には、その跡が残っており、ガイドとともに金山跡を目指します。東京都の水源でもある沢を歩きながら、水の恵みを五感で感じてください。

title: TABAワークセンター紹介動画「たばやまワーケーション」
description:
声優・雨宮天さんに、自然豊かな丹波山村でワーケーションしていただきました！

2022年6月に営業開始予定のTABAワークセンター（山梨県丹波山村）は、コワーキングスペースや宿泊もできる個室を備えたテレワーク施設です。施設の詳細情報はTwitterなどで発信予定。

たばやま観光推進機構Twitter
https://twitter.com/tabayamaksk

◯丹波山村について
東京都と山梨県の県境に位置し、多摩川の上流域、奥多摩をさらに遡り、丹波川と名前を変えた美しい渓流が流れる丹波山村。日本百名山に数えられる雲取山をはじめ、飛龍山、大菩薩嶺など秩父多摩甲斐国立公園の険しい山々に囲まれ、トレッキングや渓流釣り、キャンプなどの人気スポットもたくさんあります。古くは大菩薩越えの宿場町として賑わい、江戸時代からの伝統行事が今も受け継がれている小さな村です。

お仕事や創作の合間に村のアウトドアアクティビティもぜひ楽しんでください！

title: TABA Work Center Introduction Video 'Tabayama Workation'
description:
Voice actor Sora Amamiya has experienced a workation in the nature-rich Tabayama Village!

The TABA Work Center (located in Tabayama Village, Yamanashi Prefecture) is scheduled to open in June 2022 and features coworking spaces and private rooms for accommodation, making it a telework facility. Detailed information about the facility will be shared on Twitter and other platforms.

Tabayama Tourism Promotion Organization Twitter
https://twitter.com/tabayamaksk

◯ About Tabayama Village
Located on the border between Tokyo and Yamanashi Prefectures, Tabayama Village is situated in the upper reaches of the Tama River, further upstream from Okutama, where the beautiful stream changes its name to the Tamagawa. Surrounded by the rugged mountains of Chichibu-Tama-Kai National Park, including Mount Kumotori, Hiryu Mountain, and Daibosatsu Ridge, it offers many popular spots for trekking, river fishing, and camping. Historically, it thrived as a post town on the Daibosatsu Pass, and traditional events from the Edo period are still passed down in this small village.

Please enjoy the village's outdoor activities during your work or creative breaks!

田んぼの楽校では、田んぼと森のあるフィールド「市場」で以下のことを大切に運営しています。

●いつも食べている「お米」は小さい苗からできていることや、農家さんの作業を体感を通して学び、食べものや農家さんに感謝するきっかけをひきだす。

ただ、今年度は田植え次期にコロナウィルス感染症の影響で、スタッフのみの参加といたしました。
その際に田植えの様子を撮影しました。
また、稲刈りやはざかけ。新米おにぎりを食べる会までの映像を含めた、チャンネルユー様の番組にしていただきましたのでご覧ください。

description:
In the rice field school, we value the following in our operations at the field 'Ichiba' with rice fields and forests:

● Learning through experiencing the work of farmers that the rice we usually eat comes from small seedlings, and triggering gratitude for food and farmers.
● Experiencing that many living creatures inhabit the rice fields.
● Playing and becoming familiar with the rice fields we usually see, getting muddy.

However, this year, due to the impact of the COVID-19 pandemic during the rice planting season, participation was limited to staff only.
We filmed the rice planting process at that time.
Additionally, we have included footage up to the rice harvesting and the new rice onigiri eating event in a program created by Channel You, so please take a look.

title: 風になって、遊ぼう。～ジブリパークのある愛知～（フルバージョン）
description:
【「風になって、遊ぼう。」特設サイト】
https://www.aichi-now.jp/kaze/

【概要】
豊かな自然、モノづくりの伝統、多くの武将を生み出した歴史－－、
そんな魅力あふれる愛知県に、
2022年11月1日、「ジブリパーク」がオープンします。
「ジブリパークのある愛知」の魅力を、
スタジオジブリが観光動画として描き出しました。

作品を貫いているのは、ジブリ作品に通底する、
風や飛翔、走る喜びや、歴史を感じるノスタルジー。

ドローンによる空撮を中心とした映像を、
映画監督の中川龍太郎、
映像ディレクターのUssiy、
音楽の岩崎太整が、
愛知県を舞台に描き出します。

題字は鈴木敏夫プロデューサー、
作中に登場する版画は、版画家・宮崎敬介氏の作品です。

【ストーリー】
森の中で、旅人が残した鞄から、羽根の版画を見つけた少女。
その脇を「風」が飛び去っていく。
少女は、その「風」を追うままに、
愛知県内各地を駆けぬけ、
「サツキとメイの家」で、羽根を見つける……。

羽根を運ぶ風になって駆ける、少女の冒険物語。 

【メイキング映像】
本作の映像ディレクターを務めたUssiyが、
県内各地で行われたロケや
こだわりの編集の様子などを記録したメイキング映像。
「風になって、遊ぼう。」誕生までの日々をご覧ください。
https://youtu.be/drbaGIBw6GE

【キャスト･スタッフ】
監督：中川 龍太郎
映像ディレクター：Ussiy
音楽：岩崎 太整
出演：園原 らら（EXPG STUDIO）
プロデューサー：石井 朋彦
企画・題字：鈴木 敏夫
制作：スタジオジブリ
製作：愛知県

title: Let's Play in the Wind: Aichi with Ghibli Park (Full Version)
description:
【'Let's Play in the Wind' Special Site】
https://www.aichi-now.jp/kaze/

【Overview】
In Aichi Prefecture, rich in nature, traditional craftsmanship, and a history that has produced many warriors, the 'Ghibli Park' will open on November 1, 2022. The charm of 'Aichi with Ghibli Park' is depicted in a tourism video by Studio Ghibli.

What runs through the work is the wind, flight, the joy of running, and the nostalgia of feeling history, which are common themes in Ghibli works.

The film, centered on aerial shots taken by drones, is directed by Ryutaro Nakagawa, with video direction by Ussiy and music by Taisei Iwasaki, all set in Aichi Prefecture.

The title is by producer Toshio Suzuki, and the woodblock prints appearing in the film are by printmaker Keisuke Miyazaki.

【Story】
A girl finds a feather woodblock print from a bag left by a traveler in the forest. A 'wind' rushes by her. Following that 'wind', the girl runs through various places in Aichi Prefecture and finds the feather at 'Satsuki and Mei's House'...

An adventure story of a girl running as the wind carrying the feather.

【Making-of Video】
Ussiy, the video director of this work, recorded the locations and the meticulous editing process that took place across the prefecture in a making-of video. Please take a look at the days leading up to the birth of 'Let's Play in the Wind.'
https://youtu.be/drbaGIBw6GE

【Cast & Staff】
Director: Ryutaro Nakagawa
Video Director: Ussiy
Music: Taisei Iwasaki
Starring: Rara Sonohara (EXPG STUDIO)
Producer: Tomohiko Ishii
Planning & Title: Toshio Suzuki
Production: Studio Ghibli
Production: Aichi Prefecture

In 1535, a major flood of the Nagara River caused significant damage to the guardian's office located in Ebi Hiro (now Nagara Park in Gifu City). In response, the Toki clan moved their guardian office to Okuwa and is said to have developed the castle and the castle town. In 1543, a major battle occurred between the Toki clan and Saito Dosan, who was gaining power, and it is believed that Okuwa Castle fell.

description: Iwamura Castle is one of Japan's three great mountain castles, along with Takatori Castle in Nara Prefecture and Matsuyama Castle in Okayama Prefecture. It is also selected as one of Japan's 100 famous castles. The castle is built at the highest point among the Edo period's castle towns (elevation 717m) and is a strong mountain castle that cleverly utilizes the steep terrain with a height difference of 180m. The weather, which is prone to fog, is also utilized in the castle's construction, earning it the nickname 'Kiri no Shiro' (Castle of Fog).

description: In the first year of Eiroku (1558), it is said that Takeuchi Shigemoto and his son Shigeharu (Hanbei) attacked the Iwate clan, who held power in this area, and built a castle on Bodaisan the following year. Bodaisan Castle is a large-scale mountain castle with a complex combination of vertical trenches and deep moats. All the ramparts are earthen mounds, and it is characterized by the absence of stone walls, being said to be the most complete example of a castle built with earthen mounds.

title: Cormorant Fishing on the Nagara River Promotion Video (short version)
description: In this video, we will show you what Gifu cormorant fishing on the Nagara River is like, including the trust that a cormorant fishing master has with his cormorants and the beautiful night scene of the six cormorant fishing boats moving across the river. Gifu cormorant fishing on the Nagara River, one of the 'Three Clear-Flowing Rivers in Japan', is the largest-scale cormorant fishing performed in Japan, and one of the best parts of experiencing it is enjoying great food on the viewing boats and the company of those around you. Of course, one also can’t forget the six cormorant fishing boats traveling across the river against the beautiful night landscape. The comedic icon, Charlie Chaplin, repeatedly remarked how wonderful the experience was when he viewed it. Come experience for yourself what Gifu cormorant fishing on the Nagara River is all about!

description: このビデオでは、長良川での岐阜の鵜飼いがどのようなものか、鵜飼いの達人が鵜と持つ信頼関係や、川を横切る6隻の鵜飼いの船の美しい夜景を紹介します。長良川での岐阜の鵜飼いは、日本の「三大清流」の一つであり、日本で行われる最大規模の鵜飼いです。その体験の一番の魅力は、観覧船での美味しい食事と周りの人々との交流を楽しむことです。もちろん、美しい夜の風景の中を進む6隻の鵜飼いの船も忘れてはいけません。コメディのアイコン、チャーリー・チャップリンも、彼が見たときの素晴らしさを繰り返し語っていました。岐阜の長良川での鵜飼いがどのようなものか、ぜひ自分自身で体験してみてください！

description: This video introduces the actual cormorant fishing tourism of 'Gifu Nagaragawa Cormorant Fishing', the trust relationship between the cormorant master and the cormorants, and the ethereal world created by six boats. The cormorant fishing in Gifu City, held in the Nagara River, one of Japan's three major clear streams, is the largest in Japan, and its charm lies in the camaraderie and dining on the viewing boats. Above all, it is about witnessing the magnificent scenery of six boats right in front of you. Please experience the 'Gifu Nagaragawa Cormorant Fishing', which was once watched by the comedy king 'Charles Chaplin', who repeatedly exclaimed 'wonderful!'

【岐阜市×東京カメラ部「岐阜城　千変万化」プロモーションムービー】を公開中です！

岐阜市にある金華山（きんかざん）の頂上近くにそびえる岐阜城。岐阜市のシンボルであり、かつて斎藤道三や織田信長が居を構えたことでも知られています。

今回は東京カメラ部10選 小林淳氏とTatsuki Ito氏に、そんな岐阜城を写真と動画で撮影していただきました。

岐阜在住の写真家でも普段なかなか見ることができない角度からも岐阜城の魅力を捉えています。四季折々の風景もお楽しみいただけるインパクトのある映像になっていますので、ぜひ「岐阜城　千変万化」をご覧ください！

title: Gifu City x Tokyo Camera Club 'Gifu Castle: Ever-Changing'
description:
The promotional movie for 'Gifu Castle: Ever-Changing' by Gifu City and Tokyo Camera Club is now available!

Gifu Castle, towering near the summit of Mount Kinka in Gifu City, is a symbol of Gifu City and is known for being the residence of historical figures such as Saito Dosan and Oda Nobunaga.

This time, photographers Jun Kobayashi and Tatsuki Ito from the Tokyo Camera Club's top 10 have captured the charm of Gifu Castle through photos and videos.

They have captured the beauty of Gifu Castle from angles that even local photographers rarely see. The impactful visuals allow you to enjoy the seasonal landscapes, so please check out 'Gifu Castle: Ever-Changing'!

title: 2025年度森の京都文化観光サポーターラジオ 第3回「丹波漆＆やくの木と漆の館」
description: 京都FM丹波のラジオ番組「森の京都presents どぅゆの～？伝統文化 in 福知山」の放送音声です。前シリーズ「知っとる？伝統文化 in 福知山」から2年、今シリーズはレギュラーゲストに福知山に住むアイルランド出身のカハルさんを迎え、福知山市の無形文化財や伝統文化を取り上げます。第3回「丹波漆＆やくの木と漆の館」前半は、日本の漆の歴史や海外では漆の代わりに何が使われていたかを紹介します。後半は、福知山市夜久野町にある「やくの木と漆の館」から、館長の平岡 明子さんをゲストに迎えました。やくの木と漆の館では、丹波漆の紹介や漆かきに使われる道具が展示されている他、漆塗りや金継きの体験ができます。館ではどのような事をしているのか、また丹波漆のPRにも力を入れておられる館長にその想いを話していただきました。

title: 2025年度森の京都文化観光サポーターラジオ 第3回「丹波漆＆やくの木と漆の館」
description: This is the broadcast audio of the radio program 'Mori no Kyoto presents Do you know? Traditional Culture in Fukuchiyama' on Kyoto FM Tanba. Two years after the previous series 'Do you know? Traditional Culture in Fukuchiyama', this series features regular guest Cahal from Ireland, who lives in Fukuchiyama, and focuses on the intangible cultural assets and traditional culture of Fukuchiyama. In the third episode 'Tamba Urushi & Yaku no Ki to Urushi no Kan', the first half introduces the history of Japanese lacquer and what was used instead of lacquer overseas. In the second half, we welcomed Akiko Hiraoka, the director of 'Yaku no Ki to Urushi no Kan' located in Yaku no Town, Fukuchiyama City. The museum introduces Tamba lacquer and displays tools used for lacquer tapping, as well as offering experiences in lacquer application and kintsugi. We discussed what activities are conducted at the museum and the director's efforts in promoting Tamba lacquer.

title: 2025年度森の京都文化観光サポーターラジオ 第2回「和紙＆丹後二俣紙保存会」
description: 京都FM丹波のラジオ番組「森の京都presents どぅゆの～？伝統文化 in 福知山」の放送音声です。前シリーズ「知っとる？伝統文化 in 福知山」から2年、今シリーズはレギュラーゲストに福知山に住むアイルランド出身のカハルさんを迎え、福知山市の無形文化財や伝統文化を取り上げます。第2回「和紙＆丹後二俣紙保存会」前半は、紙の歴史や洋紙と和紙の違いを紹介します。後半は、無形文化財である丹後和紙を唯一継承する田中製紙工業所5代目・田中 敏弘 氏の娘である大森 良子さんをゲストにお招きし、和紙職人を目指すようになったきっかけや現在の心境、丹後二俣紙保存会の活動についても語っていただきました。

title: 2025年度森の京都文化観光サポーターラジオ 第2回「和紙＆丹後二俣紙保存会」
description: This is the broadcast audio of the radio program 'Mori no Kyoto presents Do you know? Traditional Culture in Fukuchiyama' on Kyoto FM Tanba. Two years have passed since the previous series 'Do you know? Traditional Culture in Fukuchiyama', and this series features regular guest Cahill, who lives in Fukuchiyama and discusses the intangible cultural assets and traditional culture of Fukuchiyama. title: 2025年度森の京都文化観光サポーターラジオ 第1回「盆踊り＆福知山踊振興会」

[Narai-juku in Shiojiri City] A very popular post town located in the middle of the Nakasendo. Walking through the streets that have remained for 200 years feels like a time slip. In the approximately 1 km long post town, there are cafes and restaurants where you can enjoy not only the taste but also the atmosphere, such as a 180-year-old traditional house cafe. There are also traditional craft shops like Kiso lacquerware lined up. A popular tourist destination that you must visit at least once!

title: 【いちき串木野市】令和三年太郎太郎祭【エアお散歩】
description: 2021年3月21日、羽島崎神社春の大祭『太郎太郎祭』が催行されました。『太郎太郎祭』は、旧暦2月4日に地域をあげて豊作と豊漁を祈る祭りです。神前では「五つの祝い」という、氏子が五つになった子どもたちが、漁家の子どもは「船持（ふなもち）」、農家の子どもは「田打（たうち）」の儀礼に参加します。船持には、船型の模型を持った子どもたちと一緒に、十数名の古老たちが特別な船歌を唄いながら境内を回ります。田打では、太郎とテチョ（父親）、コッテ牛（雄牛）が登場し、田植えの様子を方言で即興を交えながら、子どもたちや観客を巻き込んで、面白おかしく演じます。豊作と豊漁を同時に祈願する祭りは非常に珍しく、県指定無形民俗文化財に登録されています。

title: Taro Taro Festival in Ichiki-Kushikino City
description: On March 21, 2021, the spring festival 'Taro Taro Festival' was held at Hashimasaki Shrine. The 'Taro Taro Festival' is a festival where the community prays for a good harvest and a good catch on the 4th day of the 2nd month of the lunar calendar. At the shrine, children who have turned five participate in a ceremony called 'Five Celebrations,' where fishing families' children take part in 'Funamochi' and farming families' children in 'Tadauchi.' During Funamochi, children holding boat-shaped models walk around the shrine grounds with several elders singing a special boat song. In Tadauchi, Taro, Techo (father), and Kotte-ushi (bull) appear, and they perform the rice planting scene in a humorous way, incorporating local dialects and engaging children and spectators. It is very rare for a festival to pray for both a good harvest and a good catch simultaneously, and it is registered as an intangible folk cultural asset designated by the prefecture.

description:
＼Minato-iro, Roman Journey.／

The Ichiki Kushikino City Comprehensive Tourism Guide website has been renewed!

https://ichiki-kushikino.com

In addition, a promotional short movie that condenses the charm of our city has been completed.

Ichiki Kushikino City has a background as a port town, thriving in distant water fishing of tuna, and as a post town about 200 years ago in Ikki Minato. There are many valuable historical and cultural heritage sites scattered throughout, such as the 'Satsuma Domain British Student Memorial Hall' in the Hashima area, the 'Kanzaki' and 'Kanzakuen' related to the legend of Jofuku, and the newly recognized 'Kushikino Furoku' as a Japanese heritage.

We expressed Ichiki Kushikino City, where you can feel the connection between the sea and history/culture in various scenes, as 'Minato-iro, Roman Journey.'

The central lighthouse is modeled after the 'Nagasaki Nose Lighthouse,' which has watched over the safety of Kushikino Port for over half a century since 1951.

Everyone, please take a look! We sincerely look forward to your visit to Ichiki Kushikino City!!

title: 【いちき串木野市】川上踊【エアお散歩】
description: ＼見よ、川上の舞を！／川上踊は今からおよそ400年前、五穀豊穣と平和を祈念して創始されたものと伝えられています。毎年8月26日を踊りの日と定めて踊り続けられてきましたが、戦時中から一時期中断を余儀なくされます。その後昭和39年に復活して、現在では川上踊保存会によって毎年8月末の日曜日に踊られるようになりました。鉦や太鼓を打ち鳴らし踊る様はとても勇壮華麗です。※8月26日に近い日曜日に奉納・披露。今年は8月23日に開催予定だったが、新型コロナウィルスの影響で中止に。

title: Kawakami Dance in Ichiki-Kushikino City
description: Behold the dance of Kawakami! The Kawakami dance is said to have been founded about 400 years ago to pray for abundant harvests and peace. It has been performed every year on August 26, but was temporarily suspended during wartime. It was revived in 1964 and is now performed every year on the Sunday closest to the end of August by the Kawakami Dance Preservation Society. The sight of the dancers striking bells and drums is very majestic and splendid. *It is dedicated and performed on the Sunday closest to August 26. This year, it was scheduled to be held on August 23, but was canceled due to the impact of the COVID-19 virus.

description: 『七夕踊』の起源は約４００年前に遡り島津義弘公の朝鮮の役での活躍を称え踊られたのが始まりと伝えられています。太鼓踊りを中心に牛・虎・鶴・鹿などの作り物や、大名行列、琉球王行列、薙刀行列、甲冑行列などの行列ものが繰り出します。踊りを奉納する場所も多く大里地区の様々な神や先祖霊に祈りを捧げることで豊作を願っています。国指定重要無形文化財に指定されていますが、近年の人口減少や高齢化などにより『七夕踊』の存続が困難になってきており、本年をもって休止するとの発表がありました。しかし、コロナ禍により今年の開催は中止となり、来年が『七夕踊』最後の開催となる予定です。

title: Tanabata Dance in Ichiki-Kushikino City
description: The origin of the 'Tanabata Dance' dates back about 400 years, said to have begun as a celebration of the achievements of Lord Shimazu Yoshihiro during the Korean campaign. The dance features a drum dance at its center, along with creations of cows, tigers, cranes, and deer, as well as parades such as the Daimyo procession, Ryukyu king procession, naginata procession, and armored procession. There are many places where the dance is dedicated, and prayers are offered to various gods and ancestral spirits in the Osato area for a bountiful harvest. It has been designated as an Important Intangible Cultural Asset by the country, but due to recent population decline and aging, the continuation of the 'Tanabata Dance' has become difficult, and it has been announced that it will be suspended this year. However, this year's event has been canceled due to the COVID-19 pandemic, and next year is expected to be the last performance of the 'Tanabata Dance.'

Unfortunately, it was not held this year, but Ichiki-Kushikino City, known as the 'town of tuna', is doing its best to present to everyone a 'festival full of tuna'. Please come next year for sure!!

title: 【垂水市・鹿児島市】フェリー＆うどんの旅【ヴァーチャル鹿児島観光】
description: たけどんと行く！ヴァーチャル鹿児島観光/いちき串木野市総合観光案内所の名物職員たけどんが、過去に鹿児島県内を公私で飛び回っていたとき、密かに撮り貯めていた映像をお届けします。こんな時だからこそ、県内の観光を盛り上げたい！皆さんには「ヴァーチャル鹿児島観光」を観ていただき、新型コロナウィルス感染拡大が終息した暁には、ぜひ、鹿児島県、そしていちき串木野市にお越しください！！往くもうどん、還るもうどん、桜島のお供に、フェリーでうどんを。

title: Ferry & Udon Trip in Tarumizu City and Kagoshima City - Virtual Kagoshima Tourism
description: Take a virtual tour of Kagoshima with Take-don! This is a collection of videos taken secretly by Take-don, a famous staff member at the Ichiki-Kushikino City Tourism Information Center, during his travels around Kagoshima Prefecture. Now is the time to boost local tourism! We hope you enjoy the 'Virtual Kagoshima Tourism' and, once the COVID-19 pandemic is over, we invite you to visit Kagoshima Prefecture and Ichiki-Kushikino City! Udon on the way there, udon on the way back, accompanied by Sakurajima, enjoy udon on the ferry.

title: 【日置市・いちき串木野市】戦国島津詣でバスツアー【ヴァーチャル鹿児島観光】
description: たけどんと行く！ヴァーチャル鹿児島観光/いちき串木野市総合観光案内所の名物職員たけどんが、過去に鹿児島県内を公私で飛び回っていたとき、密かに撮り貯めていた映像をお届けします。こんな時だからこそ、県内の観光を盛り上げたい！皆さんには「ヴァーチャル鹿児島観光」を観ていただき、新型コロナウィルス感染拡大が終息した暁には、ぜひ、鹿児島県、そしていちき串木野市にお越しください！！今年1月に当観光案内所主催で開催された『戦国島津詣でバスツアー』の様子をご覧ください。「ひおきPR武将隊」の迫力ある佇まいと、「妙円寺詣りの歌」の笛が無限ループで繋がっているので、一度でもこの動画を観た方は、今夜枕元に戦国武将が立つかもしれませんが、霊障はないのでご安心ください！(笑)

title: Sengoku Shimazu Pilgrimage Bus Tour in Hioki City and Ichiki-Kushikino City【Virtual Kagoshima Tourism】
description: Join Take-don for a virtual tour of Kagoshima! Take-don, a famous staff member of the Ichiki-Kushikino City General Tourism Information Center, presents videos he secretly collected while traveling around Kagoshima Prefecture for both work and leisure. Now is the time to boost local tourism! We hope you enjoy the 'Virtual Kagoshima Tourism' and, once the COVID-19 pandemic is over, we invite you to visit Kagoshima Prefecture and Ichiki-Kushikino City! Check out the highlights of the 'Sengoku Shimazu Pilgrimage Bus Tour' held in January, organized by our tourism information center. The powerful presence of the 'Hioki PR Samurai Team' and the flute of the 'Myōen-ji Pilgrimage Song' are connected in an infinite loop, so those who have watched this video may find a Sengoku warrior standing by their bedside tonight, but rest assured, there are no spiritual disturbances! (laughs)

title: 世界かんがい施設遺産　十石堀
description:
【Jikkohori Overview and Features】
This irrigation facility, approximately 13 km long, was constructed in 1669 by the village head Numata Kakei of the then Matsui Village (now Nakago Town Matsui in Kitaibaraki City) based on the will and plans of the farmers themselves. Its technical features include the development of water sources by connecting two streams with different catchment areas through a waterway called 'Horikiri' and utilizing the natural terrain of the streams for irrigation channels. The area benefiting from this facility is 78 hectares, and its maintenance has been carried out by the residents since its construction. Currently, the 'Jikkohori Maintenance Management Council,' composed of residents from three regions (Nakago Town Matsui, Hinata, and Awano) that utilize the water, is primarily responsible for this maintenance.
Registered as a 'World Irrigation Heritage' in September 2019.

description: The 'Hitachi Otsu Mikoshi Festival' is held once every five years in Kitaibaraki City, Ibaraki Prefecture, to pray for 'safety at sea' and 'bountiful catches'. This grand festival, which has a history dating back to around 1726, is a major festival of the Sawawachigi Shrine located in Otsu Town and was registered as an Important Intangible Folk Cultural Asset by the national government in 2017. During the ritual of transferring the spirit, the deity is enshrined in a portable shrine and placed on a ceremonial ship measuring approximately 14 meters in length and 3 meters in width. The ship, now called the 'divine ship' because it carries the portable shrine, is pulled by the participants as it runs on land. The ship does not have wheels and runs on wooden beams called 'soroban'. This unique festival, where a wooden ceremonial ship carrying a deity travels on land, is said to be found only in Kitaibaraki City nationwide. The highlight of the festival is on the second day, during the main festival, when the divine ship makes a right-angle turn. The participants sway the divine ship left and right, changing the direction of the approximately 7-ton ship. White smoke rises from the friction between the ship's bottom and the wooden beams, eliciting cheers and applause from the gathered audience. The next event will be held on May 2 (evening festival) and May 3 (main festival) in 2024. Please come and experience the powerful 'Hitachi Otsu Mikoshi Festival'!!

description: Ajisai no Mori, located in Kitai-baraki City, Ibaraki Prefecture, is one of the largest hydrangea gardens in Kanto, boasting 1,200 varieties and 28,000 hydrangeas in full bloom. After exiting at Kitai-baraki IC on the Joban Expressway, it takes about 10 minutes by car towards Mizunuma Dam and Hanazono Valley to reach the site. Each year, from mid-June to late June, 320 varieties of Yamajisai and Ezoajisai are in full bloom, and from mid-June to mid-July, 600 varieties of Temari-type and Gaku-blooming hydrangeas reach their peak. The garden features 320 varieties of wild Yamajisai collected by the Japan Hydrangea Association, as well as about 150 original varieties cultivated by Japanese breeders, providing a stunning display of hydrangeas. Additionally, visitors can enjoy the rare foreign species Anabelle and Kashiwaba hydrangeas.

description: 茨城県北茨城市にある『和尚山』は、標高804mで茨城百名山の一つです。同じく茨城百名山に数えられる『栄蔵室』や『花園山』も北茨城市関本町才丸・小川に位置しています。北茨城ICから花園神社方面に車を進め、県道27号を走ります。花園オートキャンプ場や花園渓谷、亀谷地湿原入り口を通過し、関本町小川方面へ向かいます。亀谷地湿原入り口から約3キロ走ると、左側に駐車場（砂利敷き）、右側に登山口が見えてきます。和尚山は標高804mですが、登山口の標高も高いため、獲得標高は130m程度で、登山口から山頂までは約15分で到着するプチトレッキングコースです。花園オートキャンプ場でのキャンプ2日目にサクッと登れるおすすめの山です。山頂前の勾配はなかなかのものなので、小さいお子様（未就学児）には少し難易度が高いかもしれません。下山後は中郷温泉通りゃんせで汗を流し、旅の疲れを癒してください。

title: Ibaraki Hyakumeizan Osho Mountain: A Short Trekking Experience / Recommended Trekking in Kitaibaraki City, Ibaraki Prefecture
description: Osho Mountain, located in Kitaibaraki City, Ibaraki Prefecture, has an elevation of 804m and is one of the Ibaraki Hyakumeizan. Other mountains counted among the Ibaraki Hyakumeizan, such as Eizōmuro and Hanazono Mountain, are also located in the same area. Drive from Kitaibaraki IC towards Hanazono Shrine along Prefectural Road 27. Pass by Hanazono Auto Campground, Hanazono Valley, and the entrance to Kamegajichi Wetland, heading towards Sekimoto Town Ogawa. After about 3 kilometers from the entrance to Kamegajichi Wetland, you will see a parking lot (gravel) on the left and the trailhead on the right. Although Osho Mountain has an elevation of 804m, the elevation at the trailhead is also high, so the total elevation gain is about 130m, and it takes about 15 minutes to reach the summit from the trailhead, making it a short trekking course. It is a recommended mountain that can be easily climbed on the second day of camping at Hanazono Auto Campground. The slope before the summit is quite steep, so it may be a bit challenging for small children (preschoolers). After descending, please relax and refresh yourself at Nakago Onsen Toriyanse.

description:

description: Kameyachi Wetland is located in the Ogawa area of Sekimoto Town, Kitaibaraki City, Ibaraki Prefecture. It takes about 30 minutes by car from Kitaibaraki IC towards Hanazono Valley. After passing Hanazono Valley, there is a parking area (roadside) along Prefectural Road 27. It is located within the Hanazono Hanakuni Prefectural Nature Park and is a wetland developed in the mountainous area. Sagi-suge, Mizuchidori, and Himeichige are growing here. In the 1950s, 'Skunk Cabbage' was planted to preserve this nature. Later, the management was taken over by the city, and in 1987, about 1,000 Skunk Cabbage plants were planted. Even now, they sprout in late March, and flowers bloom from early to mid-April, attracting many tourists. *1 Reference for best viewing: 1st week of April 2020, 1st week of April 2021 (in recent years, the best viewing period has been earlier).

description: The world irrigation heritage site 'Jikkohori' is perfect for a mini trekking! Park your car at the 'Jikkohori Shinsui Park' where parking and restrooms are available, and enjoy a round trip to 'Takinokawa Water Gate' in about one hour on an easy course. Due to the high elevation, there are spots with great views and a nature-made walking path covered by earthen walls on both sides, making it enjoyable to walk. In recent years, more families have been enjoying trekking. The course is suitable for children from around 4 years old, making it a great adventure field for elementary school students! description:
The birthplace of Anko Nabe, 'Kitai-baraki City'. I ordered Anko Nabe and seafood products from a mail order site that handles 'Anko Nabe' and 'seafood products' caught at the local port.

In winter, you can sometimes find Anko sold at supermarkets in the Tokyo metropolitan area. It has an image of being smelly, and I don't know how to make it...
But that's not true! 'Anko Nabe' is surprisingly easy to make!

1. Thaw the purchased Anko under running water (if it's frozen).
2. Cut the ingredients (cabbage, green onions, carrots, shiitake mushrooms, enoki mushrooms, tofu, and any other ingredients you like!).
3. Sauté the Anko liver over low heat (if it's in paste form, dissolve it in hot water).
4. Add miso and bring to a boil.
5. Add the Anko and a little sake.
6. Arrange the cut ingredients from step 2.
7. Once all the ingredients are cooked... it's done!!
8. For the finish, add rice and chopped green onions for a porridge♪

Please try ordering and enjoy the authentic taste at home!

description:
茨城県を代表する観光地『五浦六角堂』

近代日本美術の発展に尽力した岡倉天心ゆかりの地です。岡倉天心は、日本美術の発展や文化財保護、東洋文化の世界への発信など急激な西洋化の荒波が押し寄せた明治という時代の中で、日本美術発展のために尽力した人物です。岡倉天心は晩年の頃には、この五浦の地を気に入り、弟子たちとともに移住してきました。時に荒く、時に静かに打ち寄せる波を眺めながら、日本美術の将来を考え、この六角堂で瞑想にふけったとされています。

六角堂のある『五浦海岸』は大小異なる入江が連なりできた海岸。日本の渚百選にも選ばれたその景色は、まるで一幅の日本画のようで、来る人々はその景色に心を打たれます。

description:
This is a representative tourist destination in Ibaraki Prefecture, 'Goura Rokkakudo'. It is a place related to Tenshin Okakura, who contributed to the development of modern Japanese art. Okakura worked for the development of Japanese art, the protection of cultural properties, and the dissemination of Eastern culture to the world during the Meiji era, a time when the waves of rapid Westernization were crashing in. In his later years, he came to love this area of Goura and moved here with his disciples. It is said that he meditated in this Rokkakudo while contemplating the future of Japanese art, gazing at the waves that sometimes crashed violently and sometimes quietly.

The 'Goura Coast' where Rokkakudo is located is a beach formed by a series of bays of different sizes. The scenery, selected as one of Japan's 100 best beaches, is like a variety of Japanese paintings, leaving a deep impression on visitors.

title: Hanazono Shrine: A Great Cedar for Childbirth and Safe Delivery - Recommended Sightseeing Spot in Kitaibaraki, Ibaraki - Goshuin
description:
This is Hanazono Shrine located in Kitaibaraki City, Ibaraki Prefecture. It is said to have been founded by the first shogun of the Heian period, Sakanoue no Tamuramaro, and has a long history. The 800-year-old great cedar and the old highland cypress stand in a row, and the vermilion Nio gate, worship hall, and main shrine stand out against the greenery of the trees, creating a majestic sight.

The ancient cedar standing in the precincts is cherished as the 'Cedar of Childbirth and Safe Delivery' because it resembles the figure of a mother who is about to give birth, attracting many worshippers from all over the country.

description:
This is the scenic spot 'Guitō Cape Park' located in Kita Ibaraki City, Ibaraki Prefecture. You can overlook the scenery of Guitō, which was loved by Tenshin Okakura, who contributed to the development of modern Japanese art.

Guitō consists of five bays of varying sizes: 'Koguitō', 'Oguitō', 'Tsubaki Iso', 'Naka Iso', and 'Hanishi'. It is a representative scenic spot in the prefecture, with beautiful green pines growing on the cliffs and the blue sea, with calm waves throughout the year.

Tenshin Okakura, who contributed to the development of modern Japanese art, liked this place and moved here. In 1906, he moved the Nihon Bijutsuin (First Division Painting) from Yanaka, Tokyo, to this Guitō. In Guitō, he researched a painting method called 'Bosenbyōhō' (which aimed to depict air and light) and worked on establishing a new way of Japanese painting. During the dramatically changing Meiji era, Tenshin was contemplating the future of Japanese art while looking at the scenery of Guitō.

Inside the park, there are filming sets used in the movie 'Tenshin' starring Naoto Takenaka and an observation deck overlooking the Pacific Ocean.

Additionally, there are tourist spots such as the 'Ibaraki Prefectural Tenshin Memorial Guitō Museum', 'Rokkakudō', 'Okakura Tenshin's Grave', and 'Kōmon no Ido' nearby, allowing you to enjoy the breathtaking coastal scenery while touching on the historical background of modern Japanese art.

description:

岡山城はついに改修のため閉鎖されます。
岡山忍者は、日本中にこのニュースを伝えるために裏方で活動します。
黒忍者、金忍者。この二人の忍者は、それぞれ黒と金のマイクを持ち、心を込めてバラードを歌います。
彼らの甘く悲しい声は、岡山市から世界中の人々に届くのでしょうか？

忠実だが不注意な忍者の子孫は、この街のどこかにまだいるかもしれません。
2021年5月31日に閉鎖され、2022年11月に再オープンする予定です。

title: 【Zōzan Kofun & Chizuku Kofun】~Sky Travel Time~ A Sky Walk to Experience Okayama City
description:
Zōzan Kofun is said to be the tomb of the chieftain of the ancient Kibi Kingdom, the largest in the prefecture and the fourth largest in the country, with a total length of about 350 meters. At the time of its construction, it was the largest in Japan, and its existence tells the story of the ancient Kibi's power alongside the Kinai government. From the 40-meter diameter circular mound in front, mirrors, grinding stones, bells, and a large number of iron tools have been excavated, some of which are housed in the Imperial Household Agency.

Chizuku Kofun is a keyhole-shaped mound located in Shinjo-shita, Kita-ku, Okayama City, positioned in front of the front part of Zōzan Kofun and is considered a companion burial mound. Chizuku Kofun is a nationally designated historic site and is notable for having a stone barrier with straight arc patterns carved inside an early horizontal stone chamber of Kyushu type in its round back part. It is an important burial mound that provides insight into the close relationship between Kibi and Kyushu during the middle of the Kofun period. (Chizuku Kofun is scheduled for completion of maintenance work in the fiscal year 2022.)

title: 髙橋庄太郎さんと土屋智哉さんが歩く みちのく潮風トレイル ～森 里 川 海　豊かな恵みを感じる道～
description: 宮城県出身のアウトドアライターの高橋庄太郎さんと、日本のロング・ディスタンス・トレイル文化を牽引してきた三鷹のウルトラライトハイキングギアのお店、ハイカーズ・デポのオーナー土屋智哉さん。北海道や西表島を共に旅し、共著もある仲の良い2人が、みちのく潮風トレイルを歩く旅に出かけました。庄太郎さんのゆかりのある南三陸志津川をスタートし、ゴールは絶対金華山！という庄太郎さんおすすめコースを歩いてもらいました。一度前線歩いたことのある土屋さんには、懐かしい再会の場面も！短い映像でその全ては紹介できませんが、ダイジェストで2人の歩き旅を、優しいナレーションと共にお届けします。

title: Takahashi Shotaro and Tsuchiya Tomoya Walk the Michinoku Tide Trail - A Path to Feel the Rich Blessings of Forests, Mountains, Rivers, and Seas -
description: Outdoor writer Shotaro Takahashi from Miyagi Prefecture and Tomoya Tsuchiya, the owner of Hikers Depot, a shop that has led Japan's long-distance trail culture, have embarked on a journey walking the Michinoku Tide Trail. Starting from Shizugawa in Minamisanriku, which is connected to Shotaro, they walked a course recommended by him, with the goal of absolutely reaching Kinkasan! There were also nostalgic reunion moments for Tsuchiya, who had walked this trail before. Although not all can be introduced in a short video, a digest of their walking journey is presented with gentle narration.

title: 岩間幸司写真展トークイベント〜1000キロ歩いた写真家が見て感じたMCTと三陸ジオパークの魅力〜
description: これまでいくつもの国境を越え、数えきれない街を歩いてきたカメラマンの岩間氏が2021年にMCT（みちのく潮風トレイル）全線を47日間かけてスルーハイクしながら撮影した写真展「みちのく3740～やってくる峠、遠ざかる港～」。撮影を目的とした旅ではなく、純粋に歩くことを目的とした旅。その旅の中で見て感じたMCTについて、また、MCTを歩くと同時に楽しめる三陸ジオパークの魅力について語る、岩間氏と三陸ジオパーク事務局長土澤氏のトークセッションです。

title: Iwama Koji Photo Exhibition Talk Event - The Charm of MCT and Sanriku Geopark as Seen and Felt by a Photographer Who Walked 1000 Kilometers -
description: A talk session featuring photographer Koji Iwama, who has crossed numerous borders and walked countless streets, discussing the MCT (Michinoku Coastal Trail) and the charm of the Sanriku Geopark, based on his experiences during a 47-day thru-hike of the entire MCT in 2021. This journey was not aimed at photography but was purely focused on walking. The session will also include insights from Tomo Tsuzawa, the director of the Sanriku Geopark.

title: みちのく海岸トレイルプロモーションビデオ
description: 東北、日本の太平洋に沿って1,000キロメートル以上にわたるみちのく海岸トレイル。東北には特別な景色、歴史的な伝統、食文化など、日本の魅力が満載です。多様な地理的特徴と劇的に変化する地形で構成されており、太平洋沿いの海、森林、木立は季節によってその魅力を変えます。

title: 空から見たみちのく潮風トレイル～春・夏・秋～／Michinoku Coastal Trail From the Sky: Spring, Summer, Fall
description: 普段の歩く旅では見ることのできない上空からの視点で、みちのく潮風トレイルの魅力をお伝えします。春の桜の風景から始まり、入り組んだリアスの森と海、穏やかな湾の水面に映る夕映え、岩に打ち寄せる白波など、トレイル沿線の変化に富んだ海の表情を鳥になった気分でご覧いただけます。

title: 空から見たみちのく潮風トレイル～春・夏・秋～
description: This is a perspective you don’t get to see on foot: let us show you how lovely the Michinoku Coastal Trail is from the sky. We start with scenes of cherry blossoms in the spring, then the forest and sea along the meandering ria coastline, the glowing sunset reflecting from calm bay waters, and white waves crashing against the rocks. Enjoy the many faces of the ever changing ocean along the Michinoku Coastal Trail from a bird’s perspective.

title: みちのく潮風トレイル南部～春・夏・秋～／MCT Southern Part: Spring, Summer, Fall
description: みちのく潮風トレイル沿線の自然風景、地域の人とのふれ合いやハイカー同士の交流など、ハイカーの日常が切り取られた映像です。みちのく潮風トレイル南部ならではの島歩きや、相馬野馬追まつりなどの風景も収録された一本です。（撮影地：福島県相馬市～岩手県大船渡市）

title: みちのく潮風トレイル南部～春・夏・秋～／MCT Southern Part: Spring, Summer, Fall
description: See everyday moments for hikers following the Michinoku Coastal Trail, including natural scenery along the trail, conversations with local people and time spent with other hikers. This video also shows hiking on various islands characteristic of the southern part of the trail and the Soma Nomaoi Festival, an ancient horse festival. (Filmed in areas between Soma, Fukushima Prefecture and Ofunato, Iwate Prefecture)

title: みちのく潮風トレイル北部～春・夏・秋～／MCT Northern Part: Spring, Summer, Fall
description: 木々が眠りから目覚め、生命力溢れる春から秋にかけての風景。草木は繁茂し、人々は祭りに沸き、穀物は収穫の時期を迎えます。ハイカーは移りゆく季節の中、一人ひとりがそれぞれの物語を紡ぎながら、この東北の景色や出会う人々を愛おしんで歩いて行きます。

title: MCT Northern Part: Spring, Summer, Fall
description: The trees of the forest awaken from their slumber. These are scenes from spring to fall, brimming with new life. Plants and trees grow lush with foliage, people join in passionate festivals and fields of grain are ready for harvest. As hikers move throughout the changing seasons, each person continues to weave the tapestry of their life, continuing on their journey on foot while cherishing Tohoku’s scenery and people met along the way.

title: みちのく潮風トレイル全線開通メッセージ／Michinoku Coastal Trail Full Opening Commemorative Messages
description: ２０１９年6月9日、みちのく潮風トレイルが一本の道につながりました！！環境省、東北沿岸の４県２８市町村が全線開通を祝して、皆さんにメッセージをお届けします！

title: Michinoku Coastal Trail Full Opening Commemorative Messages
description: On June 9th, 2019, the full length of the Michinoku Coastal Trail became one continuous course! The Ministry of the Environment and the 28 municipalities and four prefectures along the trail came together to celebrate the trail’s full opening. Here are commemorative messages from along the trail!

title: みちのく潮風トレイルダイジェスト編／Michinoku Coastal Trail Digest Version
description: 「海のアルプス」と呼ばれる区間を2分14秒間のハイライト映像にまとめています。波がかかりそうな海岸線ギリギリの自然歩道や真っ暗な手掘トンネル、花に覆われた小径など冒険心をくすぐられる風景が連続するほか、歩く途中で出会える地域の生業や人との温かいふれ合いを垣間見ることができます。（撮影地：岩手県普代村～岩手県宮古市）

title: Michinoku Coastal Trail Digest Version
description: See the highlights from a section known as the “Alps of the Sea,” condensed into 2 minutes and 14 seconds. Natural hiking paths come right up to the coastline, almost reached by the waves. There are pitch-black hand-excavated tunnels and little pathways covered with flowers. This series of scenes will stir your sense of adventure, while you can also catch glimpses of local livelihood and warm exchanges with people encountered mid-hike. (Filmed in areas between Fudai and Miyako in Iwate Prefecture.)

title: 地域の声を聞く／Interviews of Locals | みちのく潮風トレイル
description: ハイカーに美味しい料理を提供する人、道づくりに関わった人、休憩場所を提供する人、トレイルを日々守る人、山道を整備する人、地場産業を支える人、ハイカーを島から島へと渡す人・・・そして、ハイカーを見かけると声を掛けてくれる地域の人。みちのく潮風トレイルにはたくさんの「トレイルエンジェル」がいます！

title: Interviews of Locals | 地域の声を聞く
description: There are people who feed hikers delicious food, those who helped make the trail, who provide spots to rest, those who protect and preserve the trail each day, those who maintain mountain hiking courses, those who support local industry and those who ferry hikers from island to island. And let’s not forget the local people who come up and talk to hikers. There are so many trail angels along the Michinoku Coastal Trail!

title: ハイカーの声を聞く／Interviews of Hikers | みちのく潮風トレイル
description: 「旅って人なんですよね、人との出会いこそ旅の醍醐味。だからこそロングトレイルって、ただ山の中を歩いているんじゃダメなんですよ。地域とか町とか人と密接に結びついているからこそのロングトレイルなんですよね。」－長谷川 晋 氏／MCTスルーハイカー(2018)　「震災を経験した方と関わることはとても心に残るし、とても個人的なレベルで響くもの。ただ、悲しみに焦点を当てるのではなく、希望への物語や強靭さに関して聞くこと、人生を再生する人々が笑顔でいることなど、こういった東北の人たちとの出会いは魅力的な経験だったと思う。本当に人生を変える経験だった。」－ロビン・ルイス 氏／MCTスルーハイカー(2017)

title: Interviews of Hikers／ハイカーの声を聞く
description: “Journeys are about the people. The true pleasure of travel is in meeting people. That’s why long distance trails aren’t just hiking in the mountains. Long distance trails are about close connections with local areas, towns and people.” --Shin Hasegawa, MCT thru-hiker (2018) “When you interact with other human beings who have experienced such tragedy it really sticks with you and resonates with you on a personal level. Not just focusing on the sad side, but hearing the stories of hope and resilience, that people rebuilt their lives and have this huge smile. It’s really just a magical experience to have these interactions with people in Tohoku. It’s a really life-changing experience.” --Robin Lewis, MCT thru-hiker (2017)

title: 空から見たみちのく潮風トレイル～秋・冬～／Michinoku Coastal Trail From the Sky: Autumn and Winter
description: ドローン映像ならではの迫力ある壮大な海岸線や河口の風景、そしてどこまでも続く防潮堤や震災遺構など、青森県八戸市から福島県相馬市まで1,000kmを超えるみちのく潮風トレイルの道の多様性が凝縮されたおすすめの動画です。時々映るハイカーの小ささから現地のスケールを感じてください。

title: 空から見たみちのく潮風トレイル～秋・冬～
description: See the impressive footage we can expect from drones: majestic scenes of coastline and river mouths, as well as seemingly endless stretches of seawall and tsunami monuments. A highly recommended video because it shows, in a condensed form, the variety of the over 1000 kilometer long Michinoku Coastal Trail running from Hachinohe in Aomori Prefecture to Soma in Fukushima Prefecture. Get a grasp of the massive scale of this landscape by watching for occasional appearances by miniature hikers.

title: みちのく潮風トレイル北部～秋・冬～／MCT Northern Part: Autumn and Winter
description: このビデオでは、みちのく潮風トレイルを楽しむさまざまな方法が紹介されています。家族や友人同士で一緒にハイキングをする人々や、旅の途中で他のハイカーと出会い、別れ、再会するソロハイカーが、美しい秋から冬の風景に囲まれています。そして、美味しい冬の料理のシーンもお見逃しなく！

title: MCT Northern Part: Autumn and Winter
description: This video shows many different ways people can enjoy the Michinoku Coastal Trail. There are families and groups of friends hiking together, and solo hikers who meet other hikers on their journey and say goodbye before reuniting later, all the while surrounded by beautiful fall and winter scenery. And don’t miss the scenes of tasty winter cuisine!

title: みちのく潮風トレイル南部～秋・冬～／MCT Southern Part: Autumn and Winter

description: 紀伊水道に面し、古くから海とともに生きてきた町・和歌山県湯浅町。ここは日本の「醤油醸造発祥の地」として知られ、今も古い町並みに、発酵の香りと職人の息づかいが漂います。おいしくてヘルシーと、世界で注目を集め、ユネスコの無形文化遺産にも登録されている「和食」。その礎を支えてきたのが、和歌山の人びとの知恵と自然が生み出した“醤油”です。和食文化の原点を訪ね、醤油のルーツをたどる旅へ出かけてみましょう。

description: Facing the Kii Channel, Yuasa Town in Wakayama Prefecture has lived with the sea since ancient times. Known as the birthplace of soy sauce brewing in Japan, the town still exudes the aroma of fermentation and the breath of artisans in its old streets. 'Washoku,' which is delicious and healthy, has attracted global attention and is registered as a UNESCO Intangible Cultural Heritage. The 'soy sauce' created by the wisdom of the people of Wakayama and nature has supported the foundation of Japanese food culture. Let's embark on a journey to trace the roots of soy sauce and visit the origins of washoku culture.

description: Kumano Kodo is a pilgrimage route that leads from various places, including Kyoto, to the three Kumano shrines (Kumano Hongu Taisha, Kumano Hayatama Taisha, Kumano Nachi Taisha and Nachi San Seiganto-ji). Parts of the Nakahechi and Ohechi routes are registered as a World Heritage Site as 'Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range'. Kumano Kodo has long carried the prayers of people and guided them to a place of rebirth, known as the 'Path of Resurrection'. The grand pilgrimage journey of nobles from the capital aiming for Kumano, known as 'Kumano Gokō', is the origin of this path. This article introduces the Kumano Gokō, said to be the beginning of tourism in Japan.

title: A Journey Following the Footsteps of Kumano Gokō - Walking the Sacred Path 'Kumano Kodo' - [Visiting the Goshuin Related to Kumano Gokō]
description: Kumano Kodo is a pilgrimage route that leads from various places, including Kyoto, to the three Kumano shrines (Kumano Hongu Taisha, Kumano Hayatama Taisha, Kumano Nachi Taisha and Nachi San Seiganto-ji). Parts of the Nakahechi and Ohechi routes are registered as a World Heritage Site as 'Sacred Sites and Pilgrimage Routes in the Kii Mountain Range'. Kumano Kodo has long carried the prayers of people and guided them to a place of rebirth, known as the 'Path of Resurrection'. The grand pilgrimage journey of nobles from the capital aiming for Kumano, known as 'Kumano Gokō', is the origin of this path. This article introduces the Kumano Gokō, said to be the beginning of tourism in Japan.

It is rich in natural blessings, with many local specialties from Wakayama such as Arita mikan, Yuasa soy sauce, Kaneyama miso, the elusive fish Kue, and Nanko plum. The beautiful contrast of white rocks and blue sea creates stunning views, and the terraced rice fields that change with the seasons are also must-see photo spots.

Temples related to the warlord Sanada Yukimura and shrines associated with Koyasan in the village of Amano are also spots you want to visit.

The next morning, the view was so spectacular that we could see Rausudake, one of the hundred famous mountains in Shiretoko, making it a memorable hike.

description: 「北の大文字」は、年の暮れから年の初めである元旦午前0時、上富良野町内を一望する日の出公園の斜面に、縦70m・横50mの「大」の文字を描いた鉄杭300本に、かみふらの神社から採火した御神火を次々に灯し、雪一面の暗闇斜面に大文字を浮かび上がらせるという、雪国ならではの幻想的かつ雄大なイベントであり、今や上富良野町・富良野沿線の大晦日の風物詩として毎年、地域住民に定着しています。 今年で34回を迎え、大の文字と花火で幻想的な中にも躍動感を演出し新しい年を祝い、共に誓いを行う機会とします。 今回は新型コロナウイルス感染症の一日も早い終息を合わせて願い、無観客での開催とします。また、その様子をライブ配信することにより、全世界へ上富良野町の魅力を配信いたします。

The sacred fire, taken from Kamifurano Shrine, is lit one after another, illuminating the dark snowy slope with the big character. This event has become a New Year's Eve tradition for the local residents of Kamifurano Town and the Furano area. This year marks the 34th event, celebrating the new year with a dynamic display of the big character and fireworks. description: 北海道の中でも、一番早く紅葉を観ることの出来る十勝岳温泉。2020年の紅葉は、富良野岳方面の白樺やダケカンバの黄色が輝いて見えます。この日は上富良野町の盆地に雲海が出て、前富良野岳の斜面には朝日が差し込んで山頂から輝いてきました。いつもの年なら本当の見頃は数日で過ぎ去るのですが、今年は約2週間続きました。土曜・日曜日には十勝岳温泉の駐車場は常に満車状態で、道路脇にも長い駐車列ができていました。台風の影響も少なく、初雪も遅かったのと、山頂付近だけに降雪があり見事な紅葉が長い期間続きました。沢山の方が登山やカメラに写真を収めて見事な紅葉を楽しんでいたようです。皆さんを楽しませた凌雲閣からの紅葉もさすがに見納めです。これからは麓に向かってどんどん降りてくるでしょう。

title: 【4K Aerial】The Autumn Leaves and Sea of Clouds of Furano-dake Before Dawn in 2020
description: In Hokkaido, Tokachidake Onsen is the place where you can see autumn leaves the earliest. The autumn leaves of 2020 shine brightly with the yellow of the white birch and the daikamba towards Furano-dake. On this day, a sea of clouds appeared in the basin of Kamifurano Town, and the morning sun shone on the slopes of the front Furano-dake, shining from the summit. Usually, the peak viewing period lasts only a few days, but this year it continued for about two weeks. On Saturdays and Sundays, the parking lot of Tokachidake Onsen was always full, and there were long lines of parked cars along the roadside. There was little impact from typhoons, the first snow was late, and there was snowfall only near the summit, allowing the magnificent autumn leaves to last for a long time. Many people seemed to enjoy the beautiful autumn leaves while climbing and taking photos. The autumn leaves from the Ryounkaku, which entertained everyone, are finally coming to an end. From now on, they will continue to descend towards the foot of the mountain.

title: Have you ever eaten soba that you made yourself?
description:
Have you ever eaten soba that you made yourself?

I heard that you can have a valuable experience at Toyohira Donguri Village in Kitahiroshima Town, so the tourism association staff is ready to go!

At the Donguri Lodge at the roadside station Toyohira Donguri Village, you can experience making soba in the Toyohira style.

You can experience it hands-free as the soba flour, water, all the tools, and aprons are available at the dojo!

Under the guidance of soba master Furuta, I started making soba right away. Kneading the soba flour with my bare hands feels great!

This cool sensation stays in your memory. Knead, roll, and cut with a knife.

While being praised with comments like "You're good!" and "Delicious!", you will be making it with support.

This experience will definitely be exciting for families, friends, and couples.

You might witness a moment of new talent blooming...👀✨️

Of course, it's also okay to come alone. You can experience it as a group (up to 30 people), so it can also be used for children's associations and various group recreation. *You can make soba starting from 5 servings.

If you're thinking, "I'm tired of regular dates... I want to do something special with friends! I want to have a memorable experience with my family..." then definitely try the soba-making experience in Kitahiroshima Town.

Soba that you made yourself is exceptional.

Even just eating the freshly made soba is great👌 at the authentic handmade soba specialty store [Soba Restaurant 'Donguri-an']

title: We will deliver the coverage of 'Ask the Locals!' aired on 11/13 in Hiroshima Manten Mama 💁🏻‍♀️✨️ #KitahiroshimaTown
description:
Thank you for your patience, everyone!! We will deliver the coverage of 'Ask the Locals!' aired on 11/13 in Hiroshima Manten Mama 💁🏻‍♀️✨️

The location is 'Kobori Yakushi', about 5 minutes by car from Chiyoda Interchange. It is a historical Yakushi said to have been opened by Kobo Daishi in the Heian period. The over 1000-year-old giant hinoki is also impressive.

The mystical appearance of Kobori Yakushi (Kobori San Fukkoji) is complemented by vibrant autumn leaves 🍁 The 'Wooden Kongorikishi Statues' guarding the mountain gate are also powerful.

Although it was still a bit early for the autumn leaves on the day of the coverage, they had progressed quite a bit last week, and the best viewing period seems to be ending around the middle of this week.

When the staff took photos yesterday (11/16), there were also several customers enjoying the autumn leaves.

The guests who came for the coverage were Mr. Satake from Ball Boy and Moeko Takada.

They also introduced Mr. Corbusier and Mr. Petit Hermes over two weeks, in addition to Kobori Yakushi.

They kindly supported me when I was extremely nervous and sometimes lightened the mood with sharp comments.

Their banter was perfectly in sync, and I became an even bigger fan of both of them 😊

Please come visit Kitahiroshima Town again!! Thank you, Mr. Satake, Ms. Takada, and the staff of Manten Mama!!

description:
I heard there is 'pasta made with rice and vegetables' created by farmers, so the tourism association staff came to check it out!

I visited Nakahara Farm located in Toyohira. There are a lot of spinach in the vast area. This spinach is said to be easy to eat even for children who dislike it due to its lack of bitterness.

The guide was Mr. Takagawa, the representative of Nakahara Farm, along with his family. His second son, Haruto, taught us about the pasta. It's so soothing...

This colorful pasta was developed from Mr. Takagawa's desire for children to eat more vegetables.

They make it from scratch, combining vegetable powder and rice flour to create a chewy texture! It has a sweetness from the rice, making it easy to eat for both children and adults 🤤

Since it is processed as short pasta, it can be enjoyed not only as pasta but also in various arrangements like soups, salads, and gratins!

Enjoy the blessings of rice and vegetables grown in the same soil!✨️

The 'Kitahiroshima Town Trial Stay' provides a lodging coupon of 2,000 yen per person per night (up to 10 nights) for those who stay at designated facilities to experience life in Kitahiroshima Town or look for work and housing, supporting the expenses incurred during the stay. This system can be used to experience 'life in Kitahiroshima Town' that you may not understand in a short stay. This time, we visited the designated accommodation facility for the 'Trial Stay', BlueArtGuesthouse, with staff from the tourism association and Nakatsu from the Kitahiroshima Town Office's town development promotion section. We were welcomed by the owners, the Inoue couple. They were inspired by their visit to Chefchaouen, Morocco, during their travels and created a guesthouse themed around the color blue. Art created by their family is displayed in the entrance. The space unified in blue is so refreshing. You can feel the warmth of wood while a relaxed time flows. It's a 5-minute walk to the supermarket and restaurants are also within walking distance, making access excellent. In the spacious tatami room, I couldn't help but roll around... the smell of tatami is also very pleasant. BlueArtGuesthouse is still evolving. If you wish, you can also experience painting and plastering. Conversations with the cheerful Inoue couple are enjoyable. The trial stay allows for interaction and relationship building with local people. Would you like to 'try' living in Kitahiroshima Town? title: The Summer Tradition of Kitahiroshima Town, 'Yaeban' Festival was held on July 26 (Saturday) 🎉 #Kitahiroshima #Hiroshima
description:
The summer tradition of Kitahiroshima Town, 'Yaeban' Festival was held on July 26 (Saturday) 🎉

Arita venue, Tokkaichi venue, and Shinchi venue were all bustling with excitement.

Many stalls lined up, and children in yukata were having fun. This scene makes me feel that 'summer has come.'

As a staff member of the tourism association, I was in charge of the MC at the Shinchi venue, so I couldn't go to the Arita and Tokkaichi venues, but I was excited to see everyone's happy smiles and hear the music that was making all the venues lively✨️

The performers on stage were so powerful!! Singing, dancing, bands, and rakugo.

Seeing the children excitedly and a little nervously jumping onto the stage is perhaps a privilege of being the MC☺️

The three people who performed the familiar 'Let's go!' from the tourism association's reel video were singer caregiver 'Masashi Morimitsu,' 'Naoya Wakita,' and 'Airi.'

Their charming voices enveloped the three venues.

And the highlight of the Yaeban Festival, the 'Okabune' (land boat), is impressive and dazzling every time I see it. The 'Aritamaru,' 'Tokkaichimaru,' and 'Shinchimaru' sway up and down and side to side as if riding the waves.

I definitely want you to see it up close at least once!! You will surely be overwhelmed🔥

The grand summer event of Kitahiroshima Town, 'Yaeban Festival.' If you are interested in this video, please come next year!

description:
新商品ができたと聞いて大朝にある漬物屋「西漬」さんに観光協会職員がレッツらもー‼️

大朝にある西漬さんは創業1950年。広島で3代続く漬物屋。30年ほど前に新たな工場地と味の決め手となる美味しいお水を探し求めてこの大朝にたどり着きました。

西漬さんは新たに「地域と共に栄える」をミッションに掲げ、地元食材を活用した自社ブランドを構築するべく商品開発を行われたそう。

そして誕生したのが「広島菜」を新たな方法で製造した✨️北の舞漬✨️

1年以上漬け込む「古漬け」技法を用いて、牡蠣エキスで甘さを出し誰でも食べやすく、ご飯がモリモリ進む味に🍚お酒のアテにもぴったりです。

熟成発酵でたくさんの菌が味に奥行きを出すそう。

シャキシャキとした食感に、ぎゅっと詰まった酸味のコクとほんのり甘めの味わい。鼻に抜ける広島菜の香りに箸が止まりません。

「日本が誇る漬け物という食文化を守り、その価値をさらに高めながら未来へと受け継いでいきたい。」西漬の代表取締役 西村さんは目を輝かせながら漬け物の未来を語ってくれました。

「北の舞漬」の一つ一つの葉には、時間の積み重ねと作り手の想いが込められています。北広島町の名水で育った大朝米と、「北の舞漬」ぜひ一緒にお召し上がりください☺️

title: I heard that a new product has been made, so the tourism association staff went to the pickles shop 'Nishizuke' in Oasa!
description:
I heard that a new product has been made, so the tourism association staff went to the pickles shop 'Nishizuke' in Oasa!

Nishizuke, located in Oasa, was founded in 1950. It is a pickles shop that has been in Hiroshima for three generations. About 30 years ago, they searched for a new factory site and delicious water that would be the key to their flavor, and arrived in Oasa.

Nishizuke has newly set the mission of 'prospering together with the community' and has been developing products to build their own brand using local ingredients.

The result is 'Kita no Mai-zuke', made using a new method with 'Hiroshima greens'.

Using the 'old pickling' technique that involves pickling for over a year, they add oyster extract for sweetness, making it easy for anyone to eat and perfect for rice 🍚, as well as a great accompaniment to alcohol.

The fermentation process adds depth to the flavor with many bacteria.

With a crunchy texture, a rich acidity, and a slightly sweet flavor, the aroma of Hiroshima greens wafts through the air, making it hard to stop eating.

'We want to protect the food culture of pickles that Japan is proud of, while further enhancing its value and passing it on to the future.' Nishimura, the representative director of Nishizuke, spoke with shining eyes about the future of pickles.

Each leaf of 'Kita no Mai-zuke' is filled with the passage of time and the thoughts of the makers. Please enjoy 'Kita no Mai-zuke' together with Oasa rice grown in the famous water of Kitahiroshima Town ☺️.

(Currently, it can be purchased at the Michi no Eki Mai Road IC Chiyoda in Kitahiroshima Town and the Wasaru Direct Sales Center in Oasa. It is scheduled to be sold as a year-end gift product in 2025!)

description: Aino Sato Herb Garden is about a 10-minute drive from the Oasa IC. Over 100 types of herbs are planted in a 40,000 square meter area. There is a herb garden, a natural food restaurant, a café, and craft classes, making it feel like you've wandered into a Studio Ghibli world. From late May to late June, you can pick German chamomile. Enjoy the scent of chamomile while being gently blown by the pleasant breeze. The herb lunch eaten surrounded by many cute flowers and herbs is exquisite. The homemade herb salt goes perfectly with tempura... After enjoying a leisurely herbal tea, you can resume picking. The adorable sign dog, Ryu-kun, who loves to roll over, and the friendly owner of the herb garden make a great duo. In this grand rice planting event, the tourism association staff also challenged themselves as Hayato!!
Feeling nervous, I went to the dressing room to get dressed... everyone was very welcoming✨️

Right away, elementary school girls asked me, 'Are you going into the rice field too, big sister? Let's do our best together!' with big smiles, which motivated me.

We checked each other to make sure our outfits were not coming undone and headed straight to the rice field.

My feet got swallowed up. This is tough.
While trying not to stumble, I received seedlings and started planting. The sense of unity is fun.

With advice from the senior Hayato, when we reached about the middle, it was break time. We all enjoyed 'Bokubamushi' together.

The smell of the rice field, the pleasant rice music, and the sound of cows.

Experiencing it firsthand, I felt the preciousness of the traditions being carefully passed down in the community, and the importance of it once again.

I hope this scene continues to be passed down forever.

Thank you for this valuable experience✨️

description:
タイムスリップ！？【日本でここだけ】戦国時代の蒸し風呂体験♨が出来る「万徳院跡歴史公園」に観光協会職員が行ってきました✨️

北広島町は、中世、吉川氏の所領として栄え、小倉山城跡・ 万徳院跡・元春館跡など多数の史跡やゆかりの神社建築、伝承されている民俗芸能があります。

その中で、今回は吉川元長(きっかわもとなが)(毛利元就の孫)が建立した寺院の跡「万徳院跡歴史公園」の♨蒸し風呂体験♨をさせて頂きました。

戦国の庭 歴史館の佐々木さんに案内してもらい、いざ歴史公園へ！💨

まずは薪を割って、かまどに火をおこします。フーッフーッと火吹き竹を吹く光景は映画でしか見たことがなかったので感動…✨️

お風呂は大人4人が座って入れる程の広さで、中は45度になるそう！
マイルドな蒸気とひのきの香りが充満し、気持ちよく汗を出すことができます。

今回職員は「ゆかたびら」という白装束を着用させて頂きました。(普段着でも入れます！)

450年前、元長さんもこんな感じで蒸し風呂に入っていたのかな…と歴史に想いを馳せながら体験しました。

併設されたガイダンスホールの建物は本堂の規模を原寸大に再現したもので、展示や休憩コーナー、トイレもあります。

〜万徳院跡歴史公園〜よみがえる中世の知恵と技。
名勝庭園に吹く心地良い風は、きっと450年前も同じだったのでしょう。

歴史好きな方にはぜひ体験して頂きたいです🌞

title: Time Slip!? Experience a Steam Bath from the Warring States Period at 'Mantokuin Ruins Historical Park' - A Visit by a Tourist Association Staff Member✨️
description:
Time Slip!? Experience a Steam Bath from the Warring States Period at 'Mantokuin Ruins Historical Park' - A Visit by a Tourist Association Staff Member✨️

Kitahiroshima Town flourished as the territory of the Yoshikawa clan during the Middle Ages, with numerous historical sites such as the ruins of Okurayama Castle, Mantokuin, and Motoharakan, as well as associated shrines and traditional folk arts.

This time, we experienced the steam bath at 'Mantokuin Ruins Historical Park', which was established by Yoshikawa Motonaga (the grandson of Mouri Motonari).

We were guided by Mr. Sasaki from the Sengoku no Niwa Historical Museum, and off we went to the historical park!💨

First, we split firewood and lit a fire in the stove. The sight of blowing the fire-blowing bamboo was something I had only seen in movies, so I was moved...✨️

The bath is spacious enough for four adults to sit in, and it is said to reach 45 degrees inside! The mild steam and the scent of cypress fill the air, allowing you to sweat comfortably.

This time, the staff wore a white outfit called 'yukata-bira'. (You can enter in regular clothes too!)

I wondered if Motonaga-san also enjoyed the steam bath like this 450 years ago... as I experienced it while reflecting on history.

The adjacent guidance hall is a full-scale reproduction of the main hall, with exhibits, a resting area, and restrooms.

~Mantokuin Ruins Historical Park~ Reviving the wisdom and skills of the Middle Ages.
The pleasant breeze blowing through the beautiful garden must have been the same 450 years ago.

I highly recommend this experience for history enthusiasts🌞

description:
🍮甘いものはお好き？🍮

観光協会職員がスイーツを求めて北広島町の「にわのにわとり」さんへ行ってきました！！

横山さんご夫婦が営む、なめらかプリンと軽やかなシフォンケーキ専門店「にわのにわとり」。

扉を開けるとふぁ〜っと甘い香り。ズラリと並んだプリンやシフォンケーキに胸が躍ります。

たまご屋さんの菓子工房ならでは、お菓子達は香料を使用していないので卵の味がしっかりします。お取り寄せネットプリン部門１位を獲得されたそう✨️

シフォンケーキはふあっふあ。雲のよう。紅茶やショコラ、桜など豊富な種類があり、差し入れにもぴったりです。メレンゲクッキーやシフォンケーキのラスクも絶品です。

撮影中も終始笑い声が絶えない和やかな雰囲気で、横山さんご夫婦のお人柄がこの短い動画でも伝わるのではないでしょうか🌷
